transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-12-22 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (RetailCo Security Lead), Priya Rao (RetailCo IT Manager), Tom Brooks (RetailCo Backend)

Summary: RetailCo is evaluating Redwood for hosted + private deployment options; today is focused on SSO/SAML provisioning, SCIM sync, RBAC least-privilege mapping, and audit/logging/KMS requirements. Team wants clear deprovisioning guarantees and BYOK options.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda 

we want to run through our SSO/SAML flow, SCIM provisioning, role mapping for RBAC, and then touch on audit logs and encryption options. feel free to interrupt.
[00:23] Jared: thanks, Samir. high level 

RetailCo uses Okta as our IdP. we currently have group-based roles mapped to AD groups; we need near-instant deprovisioning for terminated users. also we have EU data residency considerations for certain PII.
[00:40] Samir: got it. lena, do you want to take the SAML/SCIM walkthrough?
[00:45] Lena: yeah, happy to. so Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SP integration; we consume the IdP's metadata and we can send an enforced NameID format or transient, depends on your setup. common with Okta is email as NameID. we also support SCIM 2.0 for provisioning and group sync.
[01:05] Priya: quick Q 

will SCIM push user attributes like department and manager? we need those for RBAC scoping.
[01:12] Lena: yes, we map standard SCIM attributes (userName, name, emails) and we can ingest custom attributes via extension fields. department/roles can be mapped to Redwood roles. note 

sometimes custom attributes from Okta need an expression mapping on the Okta side.
[01:30] Tom: what's your SCIM rate limit? we have ~10k users and several group changes during offboarding waves.
[01:36] Lena: our default SCIM throughput is conservative for shared hosted instances 

you should expect X requests per second (note: placeholder value in transcript due to noisy transcription). for Dedicated or Private deployments we can bump the rate, and we also support batching on the client side. we'll send exact rate-limit numbers in the follow-up doc.
[02:00] Jared: deprovisioning is a blocker. we need a hard SLA that when Okta disables a user, they lose access to Redwood within a minute or two. are you able to do near-real-time?
[02:10] Samir: on hosted we rely on polling/webhooks depending on IdP; with SCIM push it's typically seconds to a minute. for strict enterprise SLAs we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can run a local SCIM connector in the VPC 

that reduces network hops and meets tighter SLOs.
[02:35] Jared: ok that makes sense. what about sessions? if someone is disabled, do active tokens/sessions get revoked immediately?
[02:44] Lena: good question 

we invalidate the user's access tokens at the next token check. for immediate token revocation we can tie SCIM deprovisioning to an API call that triggers session kill on the backend. in Dedicated/Private we can provide a webhook to your session manager as well.
[03:05] Priya: on RBAC 

we want least-privilege. can you walk through default roles and custom roles?
[03:11] Lena: sure. Redwood ships with built-in roles: Viewer, Operator, Admin, Security Admin. you can also create custom roles scoped to models, routes, or environments. roles can be assigned to SCIM groups so group-to-role mapping is automated. best practice is two-tier: platform admins (very few) and per-team operators with scoped permissions.
[03:36] Tom: do you support resource-level permissions? e.g., allow a team to only call specific model endpoints?
[03:42] Lena: yes. we have route-level policies and model-level access flags. you can tie those to RBAC roles. we also support time-limited API keys and service accounts for automation.
[04:00] Jared: audit logs 

what do you capture and what's retention? we need immutable logs for SOC 2.
[04:07] Samir: we capture auth events, token issuance, admin actions (role changes, provisioning), model invocation metadata (request id, model id, latency, approximate token counts) and any admin UI changes. retention defaults to 90 days on hosted; Dedicated/Private can configure longer retention, and we offer exports to S3 for long-term archival.
[04:32] Priya: does Redwood support append-only or WORM storage for logs? that's part of our compliance ask.
[04:38] Lena: for Private deployments you can configure WORM buckets in your cloud and push logs there; for hosted we can enable write-once retention on S3 exports as an add-on 

we'll need legal on both sides for immutability guarantees.
[04:55] Tom: encryption 

at rest and in transit? BYOK?
[04:59] Samir: TLS everywhere for in-transit; encryption at rest by default with provider-managed KMS keys. we support KMS integration and BYOK for Dedicated/Private. you can supply a customer-managed key or HSM-backed key depending on your vendor.
[05:15] Jared: we need to ensure keys are in EU region for EU data. is that supported?
[05:19] Lena: yes, for Private we can put control plane and data plane into EU regions and bind keys to regional KMS. Hosted can also offer tenant-level data residency if required (we'll confirm availability in the follow-up).
[05:36] Jared: auditability of key usage 

we need to see KMS access logs; can those be piped to our SIEM?
[05:42] Lena: yes, we can forward logs to your SIEM 

CloudTrail events or equivalent. for Private you own the KMS so you own the audit trail. for hosted we can provide a stream or export into an S3 bucket and you can pull into your SIEM.
[06:05] Priya: SSO attributes 

we map groups to roles but how do you prevent privilege escalation if a user is in multiple groups? which wins?
[06:13] Lena: Redwood evaluates group bindings deterministically 

we apply the most permissive role by default, but you can configure precedence rules so an admin role requires an explicit allow flag. best practice is to avoid overlapping admin groups and use a single admin group with SCIM. we'll document precedence rules and support a deny list if needed.
[06:38] Tom: what about service accounts and automation users 

do they go through SCIM or are API keys recommended?
[06:44] Lena: service accounts are best as scoped API keys with least privilege; you can create them and tie them to a role and an IP allowlist. SCIM tends to be for human users; automated provisioning we also support via API for service accounts.
[07:00] Jared: any SAML gotchas? NameID and email mismatch issues? we've hit that before migrating apps.
[07:07] Lena: yeah, common issues 

conflicting NameID format, duplicate emails, or users without email as primary id. we recommend email as NameID or persistent identifier. also ensure Okta sends the group claims if you want to avoid SCIM for provisioning (group-in-SAML pattern). note sometimes group claims are truncated for large group sets 

SCIM is more reliable for large orgs.
[07:36] Priya: our security team will want an architecture diagram showing the SSO flow and where tokens are stored. do you have a standard diagram?
[07:44] Samir: yes, we have a security diagram and SAML/SCIM setup doc; I'll share links after the call. (link: https://redwood.ai/security/sso-scim-guide) 

[08:00] Tom: can we get a demo of group-based deprovisioning? that was asked by our ops team.
[08:05] Lena: absolutely, i'll run a short demo showing Okta disable -> SCIM push -> Redwood deprovision -> session kill. i'll capture logs and provide the audit trail sample.
[08:20] Jared: question on compliance certifications 

SOC 2, ISO 

are you certified? what's in scope?
[08:26] Samir: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; we have a controls matrix that maps controls to product features like encryption, RBAC, logging, incident response. i'll share our SOC 2 report under NDA and the compliance matrix.
[08:42] Priya: do you support SCIM provisioning to multiple environments? we have staging and prod with separate IdP groups.
[08:49] Lena: yes, you can set environment-level SCIM endpoints; group mapping can differ per environment. many customers provision staging from a subset of groups.
[09:03] Tom: in terms of least-privilege, is there an audit to detect overprivileged accounts?
[09:09] Lena: we have a roles/permissions export and an audit report that shows who has which permissions. we can run a one-off permission audit for you during the pilot and set up periodic alerts for role changes.
[09:22] Jared: data residency again 

will logs for EU tenants ever traverse US? this is critical for us.
[09:28] Lena: for Private deployments we keep data plane entirely in-region and logs are stored in-region. for hosted tenant-level residency we maintain region controls but some control-plane metadata may be US-hosted; we'll clarify exactly which artifacts are kept in-region in the follow-up.
[09:50] Priya: what about background jobs like model updates and KV cache warmers 

do they touch customer data?
[09:56] Lena: model execution only touches the request/response payload; we never use customer content to train our models. KV cache is tenant-scoped and encrypted. background maintenance tasks are restricted and logged.
[10:12] Tom: can we enforce IP allowlist for admin console?
[10:15] Samir: yes, you can set IP restrictions per role or per API key. we also support SAML session duration limits and 2FA enforcement through IdP.
[10:30] Jared: are there RBAC separation-of-duty controls? e.g., who can approve role changes?
[10:35] Lena: we support approval workflows via integration with your ticketing system (optional) and require dual-approval for high-risk changes in Private/Dedicated. built-in UI can also restrict role changes to Security Admins.
[10:56] Priya: about logs again 

what format are logs in and can they be parsed easily?
[11:02] Lena: logs are JSON structured with fields for timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id, model_id, token_counts, and outcome. we also provide human-readable CSV exports.
[11:20] Tom: for the pilot, can we get sample logs with synthetic data to validate our SIEM parsers?
[11:25] Samir: yes, we'll provide sample logs and a sample CloudTrail mapping.
[11:33] Jared: threat model question 

if an admin API key is leaked, can we do granular revocation and rotation without an org-wide outage?
[11:40] Lena: yes, keys are revocable individually. we recommend short-lived tokens for automation and rotate keys regularly. we also support key usage alerts.
[11:58] Priya: does the product support SCIM group delta syncs vs full syncs? full syncs are heavy for us.
[12:05] Lena: we support incremental/delta syncs and we can do event-driven provisioning with Okta hooks. delta sync reduces load and aligns with deprovisioning SLAs.
[12:20] Tom: any limitations around SCIM schema? we have some nested attributes for teams.
[12:26] Lena: SCIM 2.0 supports complex attributes via extensions; for deeply nested org metadata we recommend passing a JSON blob in a custom attribute and we can parse it on ingest. we'll test this in the pilot.
[12:45] Jared: curious about your RBAC UI for audits 

acan auditors see who changed a role and when?
[12:52] Lena: yes, change history is retained and linked to audit logs with a request id. we show actor, timestamp, before/after.
[13:05] Samir: ok, wrapping up technical items 

we'll capture outstanding items in next steps. any other blockers?
[13:12] Jared: timeline 

we want pilot by mid-Jan and go-live Feb if pilot OK. is that feasible?
[13:18] Samir: feasible 

awe recommend a 2-week pilot starting ~2027-01-10 to 2027-01-24. palo - sorry, pilot dates can be flexible but we'll coordinate.
[13:28] Priya: pricing question briefly 

does Dedicated add cost for BYOK or is it included?
[13:33] Samir: BYOK with Dedicated is typically included in enterprise plans, but HSM-backed key options are an add-on. we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[13:46] Tom: last question 

SAML certificates rotation, can you accommodate automatic cert rollover?
[13:52] Lena: we support automatic cert rollover for SP certs and we can work with your IdP's rotation schedule; there's a short downtime window for cert swap if not using overlapping certs. we recommend configuring overlapping cert support on Okta.
[14:10] Jared: great, thanks. can you include a sample SCIM user lifecycle doc showing create, update, disable, delete?
[14:16] Lena: yes, included in the follow-up.
[14:22] Samir: recap of next steps 

d samir send SAML metadata and SOC2 report under NDA; lena do SCIM demo and notes; jac - sorry, jared to share groups and timeline; priya to confirm data residency and KMS policy; tom provide audit retention. we'll get those artifacts out by end of week.
[14:45] Jared: thanks everyone. we'll review and get the group list to you.
[14:50] Samir: thanks all. end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-heard words and placeholders for rate limits; exact numeric SLAs and limits will be provided in follow-up security package. Links shared during call: [link: https://redwood.ai/security/sso-scim-guide], SOC 2 report will be shared via NDAs.

Recap & Next Steps: 1) Samir: SAML metadata + security diagram + SOC2 report (send under NDA) 2) Lena: SCIM demo + rate limit and delta-sync docs 3) RetailCo: export Okta groups and list of admin users 4) Agree pilot dates mid-Jan 2027
